note: Stopgap mitigations and detection signals for PHP2Shell. Mitigations buy hours, not weeks — the PHP project states they 'do not make an installation safe.' The only fix is upgrading to a fixed build (see affected_versions.json) and restarting every worker.

php_ini.effect: Closes the confirmed CVE-2026-109619 session upload-progress path.
php_ini.breaks: Upload-progress UIs that poll session state.

php_ini.effect: Removes the controllable OOM trigger for CVE-2026-109618.
php_ini.breaks: Exposes the host to memory exhaustion unless a cgroup/container cap is in place. Never pair with RLIMIT_AS / RLIMIT_DATA.

php_ini.effect: Shrinks the payload window for multipart triggers.
Disables the fatal-error backtrace use-after-free path on 8.5.

apply_notes: Set at php.ini or FPM-pool level (php_admin_value), NOT via ini_set() or .user.ini, then restart every worker. A patched binary on disk does not protect a running mod_php or FPM process.

edge.detail: Enable vendor PHP2Shell rules (Cloudflare live from 03:02 UTC release day; Fastly, Akamai, Imperva shipped equivalents). Protects only traffic that passes through the WAF. Cloudflare's CTO calls these 'a STOPGAP only.'
Every known trigger is a multipart/form-data request. Reject multipart at nginx/Apache, or allow only GET/HEAD on read-only storefronts. Breaks uploads and some checkout flows — test first.

detection_signals: php-fpm / php-cgi / httpd / apache2 spawning a shell, interpreter, or download tool
Bursts of multipart POSTs followed by memory_limit errors or HTTP 500s
Oversized or malformed PHPSESSID response cookies (memory-disclosure tell)
Unexplained PHP worker churn / frequent restarts
New .php files appearing in web roots
New cron jobs, users, or SSH keys on a web host
assume_breach_window: Any host that was internet-reachable and unpatched after 2026-10-20 should be treated as potentially compromised: hunt webshells and persistence, and rotate DB credentials, API keys, session secrets, and TLS keys — the memory-disclosure path leaks them without RCE.
